external_entities.name: calling backend
external_entities.description: An other team's backend that calls the inference gateway.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Other teams' backends call our inference gateway
external_entities.notes: The calling backend is in a different cloud.

external_entities.name: ML engineer
external_entities.description: An ML engineer who publishes model artifacts to the registry bucket.
external_entities.source_excerpt: ML engineers publish new model artifacts to the registry bucket.

processes.name: inference gateway
processes.description: A FastAPI service that receives inference requests and forwards them to the model server.
processes.source_excerpt: our inference gateway, a FastAPI service on GKE

processes.name: model server
processes.description: The service that runs the actual model on GPU nodes.
processes.source_excerpt: the model server, which runs the actual model on GPU nodes in our model network

data_stores.name: model registry bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket containing model artifacts loaded by the model server.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The model server loads model artifacts from a model registry bucket at startup.
data_stores.notes: The source says that artifact integrity is not verified: "I don't believe anything verifies the artifact hasn't been swapped — we just trust the bucket."

data_stores.name: Redis feature store
data_stores.description: A Redis store containing customer features used for inference.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The features include account age and spend bands per customer.
data_stores.notes: Redis has no password and is only reachable inside the model network.

data_stores.name: inference log
data_stores.description: A BigQuery log containing every request and response for debugging.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The gateway writes every request and response into an inference log in BigQuery, for debugging.
data_stores.notes: The log contains raw prompts, which sometimes carry whatever the calling team's users typed.

data_flows.name: call gateway
data_flows.description: The calling backend calls the inference gateway with an inference request.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Other teams' backends call our inference gateway

data_flows.name: forward request
data_flows.description: The inference gateway forwards a request to the model server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway forwards the request to the model server
data_flows.notes: There is no authentication between the gateway and the model server.

data_flows.name: load artifacts
data_flows.description: The model server loads model artifacts from the model registry bucket at startup.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The model server loads model artifacts from a model registry bucket at startup.

data_flows.name: read features
data_flows.description: The model server reads customer features from the Redis feature store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the model server reads from a Redis feature store on the same network
data_flows.data_description: account age and spend bands per customer

data_flows.name: write logs
data_flows.description: The inference gateway writes requests and responses to the inference log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway writes every request and response into an inference log in BigQuery
data_flows.notes: The logged data includes raw prompts, which sometimes carry whatever the calling team's users typed.

data_flows.name: publish artifacts
data_flows.description: An ML engineer publishes new model artifacts to the model registry bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: ML engineers publish new model artifacts to the registry bucket.
data_flows.notes: The source says it is not sure what governs who can push and thinks it may be a shared group account: "I'm not sure what governs who can push — I think it is a shared group account."

assumptions.assumption: The inference gateway presents a web interface because it is described as a FastAPI service.
assumptions.basis: FastAPI is a web application framework, and the element is described as an inference service called by backends.

assumptions.assumption: The customer features are confidential because they include account age and spend bands per customer.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the store contains account age and spend bands per customer, which are personal and commercially sensitive data.
